open_questions.question: Depth below the exact value. CD V-ditch prints 2.50 where the exact critical depth is 2.509 (g 32.2) and CD trapezoid prints 2.45 for an exact 2.456; their areas (15.6, 39.5) and the V-ditch velocity (6.3, which is sqrt(gA/T) at 2.50, while Q/A at 2.50 is 6.4) fit the lower depth. Candidate haunting for CD; to be classified, with Skeptic review, when the rebuild first mismatches.
open_questions.answer: Yes for Critical Depth; Normal Depth does not truncate. On the V-ditch, rectangle and trapezoid both modes step depth 0.5 ft from 0.5 ft, interpolate once the trial discharge passes q, and stop on the first trial within 1% of q; a short interpolation resumes the 0.5 ft steps from itself. Every field is computed at that search depth and the printed Depth is that depth rounded by PRINT USING. CD V-ditch (cd-vdit-000001) stops on the 0.5 ft trial 2.50 itself, where A*sqrt(gA/T) is 99.13 cfs (0.87% short), so Area 15.6 and Velocity 6.3 are at 2.50; the exact critical depth is 2.5088. CD trapezoid (cd-trap-000001) stops at 2.4518 (exact 2.4559); CD rectangle (cd-rect-000002) at 2.0274 (exact 2.0290), which prints 2.03. ND trapezoid (nd-trap-000001) stops at 3.2747, where Manning's discharge is 298.08 cfs (0.64% short): Depth prints 3.27 and Area 59.6 is the area at 3.2747, while CC at the typed depth 3.27 prints 59.4 (cc-trap-000001). The rule fits every field of all 53 prismatic ND and 56 prismatic CD results (quick2-solver tasks 3.2, 3.3, 3.6; results/attempts.md A-001). Recorded as haunting H-005, with the exact roots.

Sources used: (1) n for open channels (v_ditch, rectangle, trapezoid): 0.011 to 0.500, the least minimum and greatest maximum of Chow (1959) Table 5-6 as reproduced in USACE HEC-RAS Hydraulic Reference Manual 6.6, Table 3-1 (https://www.hec.usace.army.mil/confluence/rasdocs/ras1dtechref/6.6/basic-data-requirements/geometric-data/energy-loss-coefficients). The CD Area is 0.7 to 0.8 higher, which at Top Width 59.1 to 60.5 is 0.012 to 0.013 ft deeper, more than the 0.01 ft truncation allows; CD Wet Per 61.0 and 61.7 against CC 60.9 and 61.6, and CD Top Width 59.9 against CC 59.8, move the same way. So CD circle prints Depth from one depth and Area, Wet Per, Top Width and Velocity (q/A) from a deeper one. From the CD fields, q^2 T/(g A^3) is about 0.999, so the geometry is at the critical root. The printed Depth is about 0.25% below it: with the CC geometry at the printed depth, sqrt(g A^3/T) is 0.50% to 0.58% below q in all three. Also seen: CD Max Discharge (%17133, %17063, %17004) changes with q while CC prints %29399 in the same pipe, and cd-circ-000001's 53 against CC's 51 fits Max Discharge computed with the critical slope.

open_questions.question: Does circle Normal Depth stop closer to the root than a 1% stop allows? In D 2215.5 n 4.3763 S 4.641, CC prints Q %38693 at 48.90, %38849 at 49.00, %39006 at 49.10 (cc-circ-000027, -000028, -000029). ND q 39030 printed 49.00 (nd-circ-000015; 49.00 is 0.464% short) and q 39050 printed 49.10 (nd-circ-000016; 49.00 is 0.515% short); q 39168 printed 49.10 (nd-circ-000017). nd-circ-000007 (q 38986) printed 49.00 although 48.90 is 0.75% short, which a 1% stop would have taken. In D 143.3 n .0322 S 1.187, CC prints 9837.9 at 8.40 (cc-circ-000030), and nd-circ-000009 (q 9884) stopped there, 0.466% short. Measured against CC's discharge (R^.6667), the tolerance lies between 0.466% and 0.515%. With R^.667 the bounds would be 0.36% to 0.41% in the large pipe but above 0.43% for nd-circ-000009, which no single tolerance fits, so ND circle uses .6667. Stop results print Area and Wet Per equal to CC at the same depth (nd-circ-000015 and cc-circ-000028: 5693.1, 199.8). What happens when no step trial is within 0.5% stays open (new question).

open_questions.question: Circle ND when no 0.1 ft step trial is within 0.5%: how does the search continue after the first chord? nd-circ-000010 (D 21.3 n .018 S 5.2485 q 57): CC Q is 47.2 at 0.50 and 67.0 at 0.60 (exploratory 20261124-105607-af4ca8, 20261124-105607-559858), a chord gives 0.5495, and QUICK-2 printed Depth 0.55 with Velocity 87.0 (A about 0.655), where the rebuild (1% stop) prints 87.4. Circle CD: what produces the two depths? The printed Depth sits where sqrt(g A^3/T) is about 0.5% below q (a 0.5% stop approached from below would land there only if its steps were fine), while Area, Wet Per, Top Width and Velocity are at the critical root (cd-circ-000019 to -000021 against cc-circ-000031 to -000033). Is the geometry from a later trial than the depth variable, or from a separate pass? Is the stop 0.5% on sqrt(g A^3/T), 1% on the Froude number squared, or something else? Do Critical Slope and Max Discharge use the root or the printed depth? cd-circ-000010 fits one depth by the Skeptic's hand check, so the split may not happen in every case.
open_questions.answer: The two depths come from one search and a fixed offset (circle-outputs requirements 2.9 to 2.11). Circle Critical Depth searches on A*sqrt(g*A/T) with 0.2 ft trials from 0.2 ft, stops on the first trial within 0.5% of q, and otherwise takes the chord and stops on it if it is within 0.5%. Area, Wet Per, Top Width, Hyd R, Velocity (q/A, not sqrt(g*A/T)), Froude, Critical Slope ((q/A)*n/(1.486*R^.667))^2 and Max Discharge (at the critical slope) are all computed at that search depth; Depth prints the search depth minus 0.01 ft, stored in single precision. Every Critical Depth circle golden fits an offset from 0.0089 to 0.0101 ft (A-004 measurement 2). The split: cd-circ-000019 to -000021 against cc-circ-000031 to -000033 (cd-circ-000019 search depth 4.9014, Depth 4.89; haunting H-004). The step stop: cd-circ-000011 stops on the trial at 6.60 and prints 6.59. The rule was fitted on cd-circ-000001 to -000021 (A-004 H5) and then held out: the 11 A-005 cases cd-circ-000022 to -000032 were predicted in d9e1a3a before they ran, and all 11 printed as predicted, every field (A-006), including cd-circ-000030 to -000032, which print the 0.2 ft prediction and not the 0.1 ft one. No Critical Depth golden reaches a chord that is still short of 0.5%, so what Critical Depth does after a short chord is not observed; the rebuild uses Normal Depth's rule (Q-026, open). With Velocity sqrt(g*A/T), cd-circ-000010 and -000013 print 5.6 and 8.4 where QUICK-2 printed 5.7 and 8.5.

open_questions.answer: Part (2), from what discharge QUICK-2 prints 'DEPTH is Greater than the DIAMETER' for a given pipe, is answered with the rules the rebuild uses, circle-short-chord bugfix 2.4 and 2.6. The message is printed when a stored trial is at or past the stored diameter D (trial >= D) before a trial or chord is within 0.5% of q, except a stepped trial exactly on D; at that trial, when q is more than 0.5% over the full-pipe number (A*sqrt(g*A/T) of the full pipe with T = D), or under it in a pipe with no stepped trial inside D (2.4 in). So the boundary is not a fixed discharge or a fixed share of the diameter. The rules end all 43 rejection goldens that reach the search with the message (A-015; A-016 graded; A-017 graded; A-018 graded). They are the rules that reproduce the observations, not a finding about how QUICK-2 tests a trial: on the observations before A-018, 56 of A-013's 184 combinations, trial >= D (T1*D1*X2) among them, fit equally, nothing observed separated them, and the other 55 have not been run with 2.6 (A-015; A-017 graded, 3a).
